attack.reasoning: GitHub attributed the delays to increased load and hotspots on its event-streaming platform, but did not explain the source of that load. The updates neither establish hostile activity nor establish that the traffic was legitimate.

findings.claim: The initial reported impact included degraded performance for Actions, Pull Requests, and Webhooks.
GitHub reported increased load contributing to hotspots on its event-streaming platform. It was shifting traffic away from affected areas and adding processing capacity while impact continued.
The delays also affected audit log events and Actions workflow status updates. Recovery involved restoring event processing and working through backlogs.
Reported audit log delays increased from up to 100 minutes at 16:25:30 UTC to up to 110 minutes at 16:34:49 UTC, even as pull request updates recovered.
Pull Requests was reported normal at 16:33:10 UTC. Actions and Webhooks were reported normal at 16:57:42 UTC, but audit log events remained delayed by about 100 minutes at 16:59:45 UTC.
GitHub later reported reduced platform load and additional recovery mitigations. Audit log delays fell below 90 minutes, then below 70 minutes, and finally below 40 minutes.
Immediately before resolution, audit log delays were within GitHub's stated healthy threshold, but the remaining backlog was still being processed. The incident was marked resolved at 19:22:52 UTC.

The evidence points to an event-processing bottleneck affecting multiple services, rather than establishing separate failures in each service. The precise platform component and failure mechanism are not disclosed.

Backlog drainage prolonged recovery after Pull Requests, Actions, and Webhooks returned to normal. Earlier GitHub incidents also distinguish restored processing from backlog completion, but their specific mechanisms and data-loss outcomes cannot be assumed here.

timeline.event: GitHub announced investigation of degraded Actions, Pull Requests, and Webhooks performance.
GitHub identified increased event-streaming load and hotspots; traffic shifting and added processing capacity were underway.
The platform showed signs of recovery, but pull request, webhook, and audit log delays continued.
Pull request updates and webhook deliveries were recovering as processing was restored and backlogs drained; audit logs and Actions status updates remained delayed.
Pull Requests was reported operating normally.
Audit log delays were up to 110 minutes. GitHub said Actions users should no longer experience impact, while webhook recovery continued.
Actions and Webhooks were reported operating normally.
Audit log delays were decreasing; GitHub estimated another two to three hours to clear the remaining backlog.
GitHub reported reduced platform load and audit log delays below 90 minutes.
Additional mitigations were speeding recovery; audit log delays were below 70 minutes.
Audit log delays fell below 40 minutes, within the stated healthy threshold, although backlog processing continued.
The incident was marked resolved; the resolution text is withheld.

root_cause.claim: The best-supported proximate cause is a load-related event-processing bottleneck concentrated in hotspots on GitHub's event-streaming platform, producing delayed downstream updates and delivery backlogs. The initiating cause of the increased load and the exact technical failure remain unknown.

contributing_factors.claim: Load concentration in affected areas contributed to the disruption; mitigation targeted those areas through traffic shifting and additional processing capacity.
The accumulated audit log backlog sustained delays well beyond recovery of the other reported services.

open_questions.question: What caused the increased platform load, and was any of it hostile?
open_questions.why_open: The updates identify load and hotspots but disclose neither the traffic source nor an initiating event.

open_questions.question: Which platform components became hotspots, and why did traffic concentrate there?
open_questions.why_open: GitHub does not identify nodes, partitions, routing behavior, or a specific software or infrastructure fault.

open_questions.question: Why did audit logs recover substantially later than the other services?
open_questions.why_open: The audit log backlog is documented, but its size, processing rate, and any recovery prioritization are not.

open_questions.question: Were any events lost or duplicated, and when was the backlog completely cleared?
open_questions.why_open: The updates describe delays rather than event integrity. The last substantive update still reports backlog processing, and resolution text is withheld.
